# Deformation Field Parametrization

Also called: Dynamic Coordinate Mapping, Canonical Space Deformation

## Overview
Deformation Field Parametrization methods map 3D spatial coordinates from a dynamic, time-varying state to a static canonical space (or vice versa) to enable the rendering of dynamic scenes using static neural radiance fields. This approach solves the problem of modeling non-rigid, time-varying geometry without requiring a separate radiance field for every time step. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by the specific mathematical representation of the deformation field: while some use cubic B-splines for sparse data efficiency [11457-spline-based-deformation-field.md], others use MLPs guided by parametric models like 3DMMs [12044-deformation-guided-neural-fields.md] or inverse Linear Blend Skinning (LBS) with neural residuals [12724-neural-deformation-field.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family rely on the differentiability of the forward rendering operator and the propagation of gradients through the integration steps [44-radiance-field-optimization.md]. The core mechanism is the evaluation of the volume rendering equation and the computation of gradients with respect to scene parameters (density, geometry, transfer functions, camera poses) [44-radiance-field-optimization.md].

The standard emission-absorption model computes the color $\hat{C}(\mathbf{r})$ for a ray $\mathbf{r}$ as [44-radiance-field-optimization.md]:

$$
\hat{C}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{i=1}^N T_i (1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i)) \mathbf{c}_i
$$

where $\sigma_i$ is the density, $\delta_i$ is the step size, $\mathbf{c}_i$ is the color, and $T_i = \exp\left(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j\right)$ is the transmittance [44-radiance-field-optimization.md].

Differentiation strategies fall into three main categories [44-radiance-field-optimization.md]:
1. **Reverse-Mode Automatic Differentiation (AD):** Standard backpropagation through the computational graph. This requires storing $O(kn)$ intermediate states (where $n$ is pixels and $k$ is samples), leading to high memory usage [44-radiance-field-optimization.md].
2. **Adjoint Method:** Computes gradients by propagating adjoint variables backward through the rendering algorithm, evaluating the chain rule from output to input. This has computational complexity largely constant in the number of parameters, making it preferable for optimizing many parameters like the transfer function [44-radiance-field-optimization.md].
3. **Analytic Inversion / Explicit Gradients:** Uses a-priori knowledge of the DVR operations to invert the order of operations or derive closed-form gradients, reducing memory consumption to $O(n)$ by avoiding the storage of intermediate results [44-radiance-field-optimization.md].

## Subtopics

### [Spline-based Deformation Field](11457-spline-based-deformation-field.md)
This method parametrizes the deformation field using cubic B-splines with time-modulated weights to map spatial coordinates $(x, y, z)$ at time $t$ to canonical coordinates $(x_0, y_0, z_0)$ [11457-spline-based-deformation-field.md]. It enables the reconstruction of dynamic scenes from sparse projection data by combining a pre-trained canonical volume with the learned deformation field [11457-spline-based-deformation-field.md]. Unlike Neural Deformation Fields which rely on MLPs and complex regularization, this approach allows reconstruction from as few as two projections due to the efficient encoding provided by B-splines [11457-spline-based-deformation-field.md].

### [Deformation-Guided Neural Fields](12044-deformation-guided-neural-fields.md)
Deformation-Guided Neural Fields address the problem of modeling dynamic, articulated subjects (specifically human faces) in neural radiance fields by decoupling identity from pose and expression [12044-deformation-guided-neural-fields.md]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by explicitly guiding the deformation field MLP with a parametric 3D morphable model (3DMM), ensuring that the learned deformations adhere to anatomical priors rather than relying solely on unconstrained neural predictions [12044-deformation-guided-neural-fields.md].

### [Neural Deformation Field](12724-neural-deformation-field.md)
The Neural Deformation Field (NDF) is a method for modeling non-rigid, time-varying deformations in neural radiance fields by predicting per-point displacements in a canonical space [12724-neural-deformation-field.md]. It solves the problem of animating static neural representations without relying on rigid body assumptions or human-specific priors like SMPL [12724-neural-deformation-field.md]. Unlike cage-based or linear blend skinning methods, NDF generalizes to arbitrary objects and enables fine-level complex deformation through user-defined or algorithmically extracted key points [12724-neural-deformation-field.md]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like Deformation-Guided Neural Fields by explicitly decoupling the rigid skeletal transformation (LBS) from the residual non-rigid displacement predicted by a neural network [12724-neural-deformation-field.md].

### [Local Rotation Estimation via SVD](14864-local-rotation-estimation-via-svd.md)
Local Rotation Estimation via SVD is a technique used in dynamic neural radiance fields to correct view-dependent rendering artifacts caused by large rigid-body rotations during deformation [14864-local-rotation-estimation-via-svd.md]. It estimates the local rotation for each point in a deformed point cloud using Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), inspired by As-Rigid-As-Possible (ARAP) mesh deformation [14864-local-rotation-estimation-via-svd.md]. This estimated rotation is then interpolated to query view directions to "bend" rays, ensuring consistency between the deformed space and the canonical space representation [14864-local-rotation-estimation-via-svd.md]. It differs from sibling methods like [Neural Deformation Field](12724-neural-deformation-field.md) by explicitly modeling rotational components of the deformation field rather than relying solely on translation or dense deformation vectors, thereby handling complex fine-level deformations without introducing extra complexity into the radiance field model itself [14864-local-rotation-estimation-via-svd.md].
